title: Pride and Prejudice
subtitle: Jane Austen, 1813
blurb: A novel of manners following Elizabeth Bennet and Fitzwilliam Darcy as they overcome their respective pride and prejudice to find love. Set in rural England, it anatomizes the marriage market as an epistemological arena in which misreading character has real economic and social consequences. No character dies in the novel.

factions.label: Bennet Family (Longbourn)
factions.description: The family at the novel's center, resident at Longbourn estate. Their economic precarity under the entail drives the plot's marriage pressures.

factions.label: Darcy Family (Pemberley)
factions.description: The wealthy Darcy circle, including Fitzwilliam Darcy, his sister Georgiana, and his aunt Lady Catherine de Bourgh. Represent the apex of the novel's class hierarchy.

factions.label: Bingley Circle (Netherfield)
factions.description: The newly arrived wealthy party centered on Charles Bingley and his sisters, whose presence at Netherfield Park sets the novel's courtship plots in motion.

factions.label: Lucas Family
factions.description: Neighbours of the Bennets led by Sir William Lucas; pragmatic middle-class gentry whose daughter Charlotte's marriage choices illuminate women's constrained options.

factions.label: Gardiner Family
factions.description: Mrs. Bennet's brother Mr. Gardiner and his sensible wife; tradespeople whose warmth and good judgment contrast favorably with the novel's snobbery.

factions.label: Militia / Unaffiliated
factions.description: Characters connected to the militia regiment quartered near Meryton, including the charming but villainous Wickham and his complicit associate Mrs. Younge.

characters.name: Elizabeth Bennet
characters.description: Witty, perceptive, and principled, Elizabeth is nonetheless undone by her pride in her own perceptiveness — the very intelligence the novel celebrates becomes the instrument of her most serious misjudgments. Her confident misreading of Wickham as virtuous and Darcy as corrupt is not naivety but a failure of an overconfident mind.
characters.name_evidence: Protagonist; second-eldest Bennet daughter, canonical spelling Elizabeth

characters.name: Fitzwilliam Darcy
characters.description: Darcy's cold outward manner and insulting first proposal are not simply personal vanity but the collision of genuine feeling with a lifetime of class conditioning — he is expected to marry wealth and status, and his early behaviour reflects structural inheritance as much as individual flaw. His secret payment of Wickham's debts and gracious reception of the tradesperson Gardiners at Pemberley reveal integrity and generosity his social performance concealed.
characters.name_evidence: Male lead; wealthy master of Pemberley, canonical spelling Fitzwilliam Darcy

characters.name: George Wickham
characters.description: Wickham presents himself as a wronged gentleman cheated of his inheritance by Darcy — a fabrication that exploits Elizabeth's existing prejudices and dominates the novel's first half. His villainy (lying about Darcy, attempting to elope with Georgiana for her inheritance, eloping with Lydia to escape debts) is also the product of the class system: a man without inherited wealth in a society that offers such men no legitimate path to security.
characters.name_evidence: Militia officer; charming liar and opportunist; primary antagonist

characters.name: Jane Bennet
characters.role: Eldest Bennet daughter; love interest of Bingley
characters.description: Jane's gentle, charitable nature inclines her to think well of everyone, including Caroline Bingley, whose fabricated letter about Bingley's supposed plans to marry Georgiana Darcy she initially accepts. Her union with Bingley is resolved in the novel's final movement.
characters.name_evidence: Eldest Bennet daughter; Elizabeth's closest confidante

characters.name: Charles Bingley
characters.role: Wealthy gentleman; love interest of Jane Bennet
characters.description: Bingley is genuinely amiable and well-meaning, but his susceptibility to his sister Caroline's social maneuvering and to Darcy's advice causes his abrupt departure from Netherfield, inadvertently devastating Jane. He ultimately proposes to Jane upon returning.
characters.name_evidence: Wealthy, amiable gentleman who rents Netherfield Park; love interest of Jane

characters.name: Mr. Bennet
characters.description: Mr. Bennet is discerning and witty — the novel's most pleasurable voice — but his detachment is a moral failure, not a charming eccentricity. His sardonic resignation to a bad marriage and refusal to supervise Lydia directly enables her elopement with Wickham, nearly destroying all five daughters' marital prospects.
characters.name_evidence: Patriarch of Longbourn; owner of the entailed estate

characters.name: Mrs. Bennet
characters.description: Routinely mocked by the novel's ironic narrator, Mrs. Bennet's obsessive matchmaking is, at its root, a rational response to the entail that will render her and her daughters economically helpless on her husband's death. Her anxiety is real even where her methods are absurd.
characters.name_evidence: Matriarch; obsessively focused on marrying off her daughters

characters.name: Mr. William Collins
characters.role: Clergyman; heir to Longbourn under the entail
characters.description: Collins is pompous and obsequious, yet his proposal to Elizabeth carries genuine material weight: as heir to Longbourn, his marriage to Elizabeth would have secured her and her family's residence after Mr. Bennet's death. His marriage to Charlotte Lucas instead underlines the coercive logic of women's limited options.
characters.name_evidence: Pompous clergyman; Mr. Bennet's cousin and heir to Longbourn under the entail

characters.name: Charlotte Lucas
characters.role: Elizabeth's best friend; later wife of Mr. Collins
characters.description: Charlotte's decision to marry Collins for financial security rather than love is presented by Austen without condemnation — it is a rational response to a system that otherwise renders women burdens to their families. Elizabeth's horror at Charlotte's choice is itself a form of privilege available only because Elizabeth's father is still living.
characters.name_evidence: Elizabeth's pragmatic best friend; daughter of Sir William Lucas; later Charlotte Collins

characters.name: Lady Catherine de Bourgh
characters.role: Darcy's aunt; Collins's patroness; mistress of Rosings Park
characters.description: Lady Catherine is imperious and accustomed to unquestioned deference; her visit to warn Elizabeth away from Darcy backfires when Elizabeth refuses to comply. Ironically, Lady Catherine's account of Elizabeth's defiance to Darcy gives him hope that Elizabeth has changed her feelings, precipitating his second proposal.
characters.name_evidence: Darcy's domineering aunt; Collins's patroness; mistress of Rosings Park

characters.name: Caroline Bingley
characters.description: Caroline is a social climber who pursues Darcy while systematically undermining Elizabeth's standing. Her fabricated letter to Jane — claiming Bingley will marry Georgiana Darcy — is a deliberate act of sabotage that temporarily succeeds in separating the couple.
characters.name_evidence: Bingley's younger sister; social climber who pursues Darcy and undermines Elizabeth

characters.name: Lydia Bennet
characters.description: Lydia's reckless elopement with Wickham — enabled by Mr. Bennet's failure to supervise her — threatens the marital prospects of all her sisters and is only resolved by Darcy's secret financial intervention. She ends the novel married to Wickham and financially dependent on Darcy and the Bennet family.
characters.name_evidence: Youngest, most irresponsible Bennet daughter; elopes with Wickham

characters.name: Mrs. Gardiner
characters.description: Mrs. Gardiner serves as a grounding, judicious influence on Elizabeth and Jane, offering counsel that contrasts with Mrs. Bennet's anxious scheming. Her letter to Elizabeth reveals Darcy's true role in resolving the Lydia-Wickham crisis.
characters.name_evidence: Mrs. Bennet's sister-in-law; sensible maternal figure to Elizabeth and Jane

characters.name: Mr. Edward Gardiner
characters.role: Merchant; uncle to Elizabeth and Jane
characters.description: A successful and decent tradesperson whose good sense and social warmth are notable given Darcy's class prejudices. He is actively involved in the effort to find Lydia after her elopement, though the financial resolution of that crisis is ultimately Darcy's doing.
characters.name_evidence: Mrs. Bennet's brother; successful merchant; instrumental in resolving the Lydia-Wickham crisis

characters.name: Georgiana Darcy
characters.description: Georgiana is shy and gentle; her near-elopement with Wickham — who targeted her inheritance — is the backstory that reveals both Wickham's true character and Darcy's protective loyalty to his family.
characters.name_evidence: Darcy's shy, younger sister; nearly eloped with Wickham before Darcy intervened

characters.name: Colonel Fitzwilliam
characters.role: Darcy's cousin; co-guardian of Georgiana Darcy
characters.description: An agreeable and candid man whose conversations with Elizabeth at Rosings inadvertently reveal Darcy's role in separating Bingley from Jane, temporarily deepening Elizabeth's prejudice against Darcy.
characters.name_evidence: Darcy's cousin; co-guardian of Georgiana; younger son of an earl

characters.name: Mary Bennet
characters.description: Mary is the most studious and moralistic of the Bennet sisters, prone to pedantic pronouncements that Austen deploys for gentle comedy.
characters.name_evidence: Third Bennet daughter; bookish and moralistic

characters.name: Catherine "Kitty" Bennet
characters.description: Kitty largely follows Lydia's example in her enthusiasm for the militia officers, playing a minor role in the social texture of Meryton life.
characters.name_evidence: Fourth Bennet daughter; follows Lydia's lead in flirting with soldiers

characters.name: Mrs. Younge
characters.description: Mrs. Younge facilitated Wickham's access to Georgiana during the attempted elopement, making her complicit in what amounted to a scheme to steal Georgiana's inheritance.
characters.name_evidence: Georgiana's former companion; complicit in Wickham's attempted elopement

characters.name: Mrs. Reynolds
characters.description: Mrs. Reynolds's warm and unsolicited praise of Darcy's character during Elizabeth's visit to Pemberley constitutes some of the novel's most persuasive evidence of his genuine integrity — testimony from a dependent who has no motive to flatter.
characters.name_evidence: Darcy's housekeeper at Pemberley; speaks highly of his character to Elizabeth

coverage_note: Mr. and Mrs. Phillips, Mrs. Louisa Hurst, Sir William Lucas, and Anne de Bourgh are listed in the analysis Cast section but omitted here as the 20-character cap was reached with characters of greater narrative function. All 20 slots are filled by characters whose roles drive plot or theme.
adaptation_note: The 1995 BBC miniseries is an almost exact page-for-page adaptation, preserving minor characters and subplots the 2005 film omits or compresses. The 2005 film shifts the setting to the 1790s, softens Mr. and Mrs. Bennet into more sympathetic figures, and ends with an intimate post-marriage Pemberley scene rather than the novel's broader social resolution — a conclusion that caused substantial controversy and exists in different versions for the UK and US releases.
notes: Character map generated from the verified spoiler-complete analysis. Spoiler levels reflect the novel's sustained epistemological misdirection around Wickham and Darcy: Wickham's villainy (level 2) is revealed mid-novel via Darcy's letter; the full resolution of the Lydia crisis, Darcy's secret financial intervention, and Lady Catherine's inadvertent role in the second proposal are level 3. No character dies in the novel.
